lines.trans: Andrea, we have a big problem with the casting.
What is going on with the film?
I made a huge mistake.
Bassem is not Baptiste.
What do you mean? Baptiste is forty-five years old!
Yes, it is a very important role.
He is the main partner of Gerard Lanvin.
But how could you confuse the two?
The two first names sound too much alike.
Did you try calling Mathias?
Yes, I reached his voicemail.
We must find a solution right away.
I am going to try to fix my mistake.
Hurry up, the casting is starting now.

lines.trans: I am going to try to fix my mistake.

examples.text: Ça va? Oui, ça va bien.
examples.trans: How are you? Yes, I'm fine.

meanings.note: aller + infinitive: tu vas l'agacer = you're going to annoy her
ça va? = how are you? / are you okay?
with numbers: huit ans, vingt ans

examples.text: Appelle Clémentine. Dis-lui que je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
examples.trans: Call Clémentine. Tell her I can't come tonight.

meanings.note: je peux t'appeler? = can I call you?

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

examples.text: Il y a un macaron sur la table.
examples.trans: There's a macaron on the table.

meanings.note: avoir peur = to be afraid, avoir raison = to be right, avoir 40 ans = to be 40
elle a quarante ans = she is forty

meanings.en: il y a = there is / there are

examples.text: Dis bonjour à Mathias. Mais c'est quoi ces bêtises?
examples.trans: Say hello to Mathias. Hey, what is this nonsense?

meanings.note: dire des bêtises = to talk nonsense / say rude things

examples.text: Elle me veut pour le casting!
examples.trans: She wants me for the casting!

examples.text: Oui! Et elle me veut pour le casting!
examples.trans: Yes! And she wants me for the casting!

meanings.en: casting, audition process (for a film or play)

meanings.note: before a noun: ce film, cette tête, ces gens
as a pronoun in c'est, ce n'est pas; becomes c' before a vowel

examples.text: Elles commencent avec un peu de Botox.
examples.trans: They start with a bit of Botox.

meanings.note: commencer + noun, or commencer à + infinitive

meanings.en: commencer par / avec: to start with

meanings.note: comment ça va? = how are you?

meanings.en: to confuse, to mistake one thing for another

examples.text: Vous confondez vie privée et vie professionnelle.
examples.trans: You confuse private life and professional life.

examples.text: Tu confonds la fiction et la réalité.
examples.trans: You are confusing fiction and reality.

examples.text: Je confonds le poivre et le sel aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: I confuse the pepper and the salt today.

examples.text: La plus grande imprésario de Paris.

meanings.note: je n'ai pas de temps; also before a plural adjective: de mauvaises nouvelles

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: the x sounds like z before a vowel

meanings.en: to hurry, to rush; se dépêcher = to hurry up
meanings.note: First-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are'), the most productive verb class in French. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Core French verb meaning 'to hurry, to rush'.

examples.text: Il faut se dépêcher, c'est loin.
examples.trans: We must hurry, it is far.
This way, let us hurry up a bit!
Hurry up, the casting is starting now.

examples.text: Ce tournage était une grande erreur.
examples.trans: This shoot was a big mistake.

examples.text: J'ai commis une grave erreur il y a vingt-quatre ans.
examples.trans: I made a serious mistake twenty-four years ago.

examples.text: J'ai essayé de t'appeler. C'est non-stop au boulot aujourd'hui.
examples.trans: I tried to call you. It's non-stop at work today.

meanings.note: pour faire quoi? = to do what?
faire du vélo = to ride a bike, to cycle

falloir.governs: il faut + infinitive, or il faut que + subjunctive

meanings.note: only with the impersonal 'il': il faut
il me faut un stylo = I need a pen

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.
On a perdu un gros contrat.

meanings.note: before the noun: un gros contrat
for masculine nouns, and in impersonal phrases: il y a
Prefix 'im-' marks negation ('un-, im-') or inward motion.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: before the verb: vous la connaissez? les voilà

examples.text: Très bien. Tu peux commencer maintenant?
examples.trans: Very good. Can you start now?

examples.text: Je veux, mais je ne peux pas.
examples.trans: I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Vous êtes sur la messagerie de Mathias.
Laissez un mot sur ma messagerie.
examples.trans: Leave a note on my voicemail.

examples.text: Oui, je suis tombé sur sa messagerie.

meanings.note: ne ... pas: not; ne ... plus: not anymore; ne ... jamais: never

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: everyday speech, with a he/she verb form

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

examples.text: C'est ma partenaire dans le film.
examples.trans: She is my co-star in the movie.
He wants to choose his partners.

meanings.note: same form for masculine and feminine

meanings.en: pas du tout: not at all

examples.trans: I can't take it any more.

meanings.note: je peux t'appeler? = may I call you?
je n'en peux plus = I can't take any more

examples.text: Vous êtes toujours sûr pour le rôle principal féminin?
examples.trans: Are you still sure about the female lead?

meanings.note: le rôle principal = the lead role
choisir un prénom = to choose a first name

examples.text: Pourquoi as-tu choisi le prénom Chantal?
examples.trans: Why did you choose the first name Chantal?

examples.text: Gabriel? Qu'est-ce qui se passe ici?

meanings.note: question word when 'what' is the subject: qu'est-ce qui se passe? = what's happening?

examples.text: Il a quarante-cinq ans dans le scénario.
examples.trans: He is forty-five years old in the script.

examples.text: Comment ça? Baptiste a quarante-cinq ans!
examples.trans: What do you mean? Baptiste is forty-five years old!
But you really look like him!

examples.text: Mais tu lui ressembles vraiment! Je suis vraiment désolée!
examples.trans: But you really look like him! I'm really sorry!

meanings.note: ressembler à quelqu'un = to look like someone (indirect object: lui ressembler)

examples.text: Et j'ai réparé son chemisier préféré.
examples.trans: And I fixed her favourite blouse.

meanings.en: to repair, to fix, to mend
meanings.note: First-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are'), the most productive verb class in French. Prefix 'ré-' marks repetition, return, or intensity. Core French verb meaning 'to repair, to fix'.

examples.text: Oui! Mon préféré, Pierre Niney, a un nouveau rôle.
examples.trans: Yes! My favourite, Pierre Niney, has a new part.

meanings.en: part, role (in a film or play)

examples.text: Une solution? Une grande actrice de quatre-vingts ans, libre dans trois semaines?
examples.trans: A solution? A great eighty-year-old actress, free in three weeks?

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'solution, answer'.

examples.text: Oui, trois cent mille. Je parle de ses vingt ans de carrière.
examples.trans: Yes, three hundred thousand. I'm talking about his twenty years of career.

meanings.note: agrees with the thing owned, not the owner

examples.text: Le livre est sur la table.
examples.trans: The book is on the table.

examples.text: Attention, tu arrives sur la route!
examples.trans: Careful, you're heading for the road!

meanings.note: sur la table, sur la route

examples.text: Il est tombé dans la rue.

meanings.en: laisser tomber = to drop it, to forget it

examples.trans: All right, I am coming right away.

meanings.note: Everyday French tudəsɥit meaning 'right away, immediately'.

examples.text: Elle est trop vieille pour le rôle.
examples.trans: She's too old for the part.

examples.text: Trop vieille? C'est quoi le rôle, une gamine?
examples.trans: Too old? What's the part, a little girl?

examples.text: Je ne sais pas. Trouve quelque chose.
examples.trans: I don't know. Think of something.

meanings.note: trouver quelqu'un sympa = to find someone nice

meanings.en: trouve quelque chose = think of something

examples.text: Très bien. Et vous? Un thé?

meanings.note: singular and informal: friends, family, children, colleagues of the same age

examples.text: Nous avons fait un énorme effort, Hélène.
examples.trans: We've made a huge effort, Hélène.
